r2.current_hypothesis: Humans deviate strongly from EV maximization.
r2.key_evidence: corr(evB-evA, P(B)) = +0.037 (essentially ZERO). EV-argmax matches the human MAJORITY choice on only 48.6% of trials (worse than a coin flip / the 68% base-rate of choosing B). Binned P(B) vs mean EV-diff is U-SHAPED, not monotonic: P(B)=0.77 when B is much WORSE (EVdiff -11.7), 0.64 near EVdiff~0, and 0.77 when B is much BETTER (EVdiff +11.7). So choice tracks the MAGNITUDE |EV diff| (stakes/discriminability), not its SIGN. Signed EV advantage carries almost no weight in human choice here.
r2.main_risk: Strong B-bias inflates base rate; the U-shape may reflect that large-EV-gap items are also high-variance/skew items where probability-weighting effects dominate.
r2.next_action: Conclude Q1 and use this as the yardstick for Q2 (does an LLM track EV or this human pattern?).
